messages:
zoe: Hi all 44b Im on my first day and hit a bootstrap snag. Ran the dotfiles ./bootstrap (macOS corporate laptop) but my asdf shims arent taking effect and `pnpm` is missing. `which asdf` -> /opt/homebrew/bin/asdf, `which pnpm` -> not found. Im not sure if Homebrew is expected at /opt/homebrew or /usr/local on these laptops. Any quick triage tips?

priya: welcome! :tada: Quick checks: `echo $SHELL`, `echo $PATH`, and `cat ~/.tool-versions` if present. Also did the bootstrap create `~/.dotfiles` symlink or copy?

zoe: `echo $SHELL` -> /bin/zsh. `echo $PATH` shows /usr/bin before /Users/zoe/.asdf/shims. `~/.tool-versions` is empty. The bootstrap did symlink `~/.zshrc` to our dotfiles. The top of my zshrc has `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"` but no `asdf.sh` sourcing lines.

dan: since shims are after /usr/bin they'll be shadowed. Add the `asdf.sh` lines and ensure they run before other PATH tweaks. In our zshrc we keep these at the very top:```
# asdf
. $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh
. $(brew --prefix asdf)/etc/profile.d/asdf.sh
export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"
```

zoe: added them and restarted shell. `asdf list` is empty and `asdf plugin-list` shows `python nodejs`. Trying `asdf install python 3.10.12` errors on compile with openssl headers missing.

priya: classic mac dev libs issue. Run `brew install openssl readline xz zlib`. Then export build flags before install:```
export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl)/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl)/include"
asdf install python 3.10.12
```If `brew --prefix` gives /opt/homebrew thats fine regardless of CPU arch — the important bit is `$(brew --prefix openssl)` in the flags.

zoe: brew install finished but `brew --prefix` -> /opt/homebrew even though About says Intel. Is that ok? The corporate image may have had an arm brew installed earlier.

dan: it's okay to use whichever brew install exists, but we should document the intel vs arm gotcha. For intel machines we usually expect /usr/local, but `$(brew --prefix)` keeps things portable. Also check if MDM or a security profile blocked writing to /usr/local; that can cause weird residual installs.

zoe: after setting LDFLAGS/CPPFLAGS as suggested the python build succeeded. Reinstalled `pnpm` with `npm i -g pnpm` but it still landed in /usr/local/bin/pnpm and I had to use sudo. How do I make npm globals go into my home dir?

priya: set an npm prefix in your home dir:```mkdir -p "$HOME/.npm-global"
npm config set prefix "$HOME/.npm-global"
export PATH="$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"```Add the PATH line to your zshrc before other PATH overrides and reopen shell, then `npm i -g pnpm` will put pnpm under ~/.npm-global/bin.

zoe: did that and `which pnpm` -> /Users/zoe/.npm-global/bin/pnpm. Also ran `direnv allow` in the repo and now `asdf current` shows python 3.10.12. Everything green.

infra-bot: Ticket INF-860 created: "onboarding: clarify Homebrew prefix and npm global prefix in dotfiles README" assigned to @priya.

zoe: huge thanks everyone! Ill send a quick PR to the dotfiles README with notes about brew prefix, LDFLAGS for python builds, and npm prefix ordering.
